environment.tool: manual review of the release tag + live compiled binary against a two-root kv config

findings.description: The local branch picks root from the vhost pair then replaces it with the alias root when the decoded path matches the alias prefix. Host validation is already finished, so nothing re-checks the alias root against the winning vhost. Controls: alpha root 200 and an alpha-only file 404 on the beta vhost; then GET /alias/hello.txt on the beta vhost returns the alias file. Read-scope bypass; RCE-adjacent if the alias root holds an executable the upstream would run.
findings.title: The alias branch overwrites the vhost-selected document root after host validation, so a confined vhost reads the alias root

findings.description: GET /alias%2fhello.txt returns the same file because the compare is on the decoded path. Anything inspecting the raw URL first sees an unrelated prefix.
findings.title: The alias prefix is matched on the decoded path, so the %2f spelling reaches the same alias root and defeats a raw-prefix check in front of the proxy

limitations: No executor in the alias root here
methods: Read the release source from the tag
Marked distinct content in alpha, beta and alias roots
Confirmed beta confinement with an alpha-only file
Drove alias plainly and with %2f from the beta vhost
